---

## Critical

**`/C/Users/filip/AppData/Local/Temp/leverage-audit-default-audit-default-2026-05-24/C.code-reviewer__leveraged-forced__r1/work/service/routes/users.py:16`** — SQL injection via f-string query construction

What: `user_id` is taken directly from `request.query` and interpolated into a raw SQL string with no sanitization or parameterization. An attacker can supply a value like `' OR '1'='1` to read arbitrary rows, or more destructive payloads depending on the SQLite configuration.

Why: This is a textbook SQL injection vulnerability. The `_ID_PATTERN` validator exists in `service/validator.py` specifically for this purpose but is never called here, leaving the guard completely unused.

Suggested direction: Replace the f-string with a parameterized query using the `?` placeholder (`"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = ?"`, `(user_id,)`), and call `is_valid_id(user_id)` before executing — returning a 400 if validation fails.

---

**`/C/Users/filip/AppData/Local/Temp/leverage-audit-default-audit-default-2026-05-24/C.code-reviewer__leveraged-forced__r1/work/service/routes/users.py:14`** — Missing null/missing-key guard on `user_id`

What: `request.query.get("id")` returns `None` when the `id` parameter is absent. `None` is then interpolated directly into the SQL string as the literal string `'None'`, producing a silent wrong-result query rather than a validation error. The validator's `is_valid_id` already handles `None` correctly, but it is not invoked.

Why: A caller omitting the `id` parameter gets a 404 instead of a 400, masking the real error. With parameterized queries the same `None` would be passed as SQL NULL and also silently miss — so the guard must happen before the query regardless of which SQL fix is applied.

Suggested direction: After `get("id")`, check `is_valid_id(user_id)` and return `{"status": 400, "body": {"error": "invalid id"}}` on failure, before touching the database.

---

**`/C/Users/filip/AppData/Local/Temp/leverage-audit-default-audit-default-2026-05-24/C.code-reviewer__leveraged-forced__r1/work/service/routes/users.py:7`** — Module-level mutable shared SQLite connection

What: `_DB = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")` is created once at import time and shared across all requests. `sqlite3` connections are not thread-safe by default (`check_same_thread=True` is the default and will raise if the connection is used from a different thread than the one that created it). In any multi-threaded server environment this will raise `ProgrammingError` at runtime.

Why: The module is imported once; the connection is owned by the importing thread. Any framework that dispatches requests on a thread pool will immediately hit the thread-safety violation.

Suggested direction: Either pass `check_same_thread=False` and add a threading lock around all cursor use, or (preferred) create a per-request connection or use a proper connection pool. Since the DB is in-memory and used only in tests right now, the simplest correctness fix is to acknowledge the constraint explicitly and add a lock.

---

## Important

**`/C/Users/filip/AppData/Local/Temp/leverage-audit-default-audit-default-2026-05-24/C.code-reviewer__leveraged-forced__r1/work/service/validator.py`** — `is_valid_id` is dead code in production paths

What: The validator module is staged as a new file but nothing in the staged routes imports or uses it. It is only indirectly useful if the callers are fixed (see Critical findings above).

Why: Dead code that was clearly written to solve an existing problem signals the fix is incomplete. Reviewers and future contributors may not realize the validator is meant to be the gate for `get_user`.

Suggested direction: Wire `is_valid_id` into `get_user` as part of the same PR that introduces it, so the module is never merged in an unused state.

---

**`/C/Users/filip/AppData/Local/Temp/leverage-audit-default-audit-default-2026-05-24/C.code-reviewer__leveraged-forced__r1/work/tests/test_users.py`** — No test coverage for invalid / missing `id` parameter

What: The test file covers the happy path and the auth guard, but there are no tests for: missing `id` query param, an `id` that fails the pattern (e.g. SQL metacharacters), or a valid-format id that does not exist in the DB (404 path).

Why: The 404 branch and the validation branch are the exact paths where the Critical bugs above live. Without tests for them, regressions will go undetected.

Suggested direction: Add test cases for `qid=None`, `qid="' OR '1'='1"`, and `qid="999"` (unknown user), asserting 400, 400, and 404 respectively.

---

**`/C/Users/filip/AppData/Local/Temp/leverage-audit-default-audit-default-2026-05-24/C.code-reviewer__leveraged-forced__r1/work/service/auth.py:9`** — Auth check is presence-only, not value-validated

What: `require_auth` passes any non-empty `Authorization` header value, including `"Bearer "` (empty token), `"garbage"`, or `"Bearer wrong"`. The test in `test_users.py` uses `"Bearer test"` which would pass in production.

Why: This is an existing limitation noted here for awareness because the new route relies on it and the new tests reinforce the pattern. It is not introduced by this PR but the PR propagates the same weak check without comment.

Suggested direction: Consider a follow-up issue to validate the token value, or at minimum document that `require_auth` is a placeholder and not production-strength.

---

## Nice to have

**`/C/Users/filip/AppData/Local/Temp/leverage-audit-default-audit-default-2026-05-24/C.code-reviewer__leveraged-forced__r1/work/tests/test_users.py:4`** — `_Req` stub duplicated from `test_status.py`

What: Both test files define an identical `_Req` helper class. They differ only in whether `query` defaults to `{}` or is populated from a `qid` argument.

Why: Minor duplication; not a bug. If the request interface changes, both stubs need updating.

Suggested direction: Extract a shared `_Req` factory into `tests/__init__.py` or a `tests/conftest.py` (if pytest is the runner) so there is a single definition to maintain.
